content_voiceover: This algorithm walks through CMML risk-adapted management, referencing a 2022 Haematologica risk model. Median overall survival ranges dramatically by risk group, from ninety seven months in low risk down to just sixteen months in high risk disease. Low risk patients without autoimmune features are simply observed, though autoimmune manifestations may warrant prednisone, anti-cytokine agents, or DNA methyltransferase inhibitors. For high risk and intermediate-2 risk patients, allogeneic stem cell transplant is the preferred curative approach whenever the patient is eligible. Transplant-ineligible patients are then split by CMML subtype, dysplastic CMML with TET2 mutated, ASXL1 wild type biology is managed with DNA methyltransferase inhibitors, while proliferative CMML, marked by ASXL1 or RAS pathway mutations, is steered toward clinical trials targeting pathways like MEK, PLK1, CD123, or GM-CSF signaling. Intermediate-1 risk and symptomatic intermediate-2 patients get treatment tailored to their dominant problem, erythropoiesis stimulating agents or luspatercept for anemia, hydroxyurea or off-label ruxolitinib for splenomegaly or constitutional symptoms, and for thrombocytopenia, options range from clinical trials in proliferative disease to immune-mediated therapies like rituximab, eltrombopag, or romiplostim.
keypoints: CMML risk stratifies from median OS 97 months (low) to 16 months (high)
High and intermediate-2 risk: allogeneic transplant if eligible
Transplant-ineligible: DNMTi for dysplastic CMML, clinical trials for proliferative CMML
Symptom-directed therapy for intermediate-1 risk: anemia, splenomegaly, thrombocytopenia each have distinct options
keypoint_voiceover: The core logic, risk stratify first using the survival-based model, send high and intermediate-2 risk patients to transplant if eligible, and if not, split by dysplastic versus proliferative biology for DNMTi versus clinical trials. Lower risk or symptomatic intermediate-1 disease gets managed by dominant symptom, anemia, splenomegaly, or thrombocytopenia, each with its own directed therapy.
